note: Venture packages (EE-067, EE-069): the venture's business source of truth, grouped two ways. Core packages are where the records live, one per department (EE-047) plus the foundation; every record has exactly one home and other packages read it (refs). Handoff packages hold no records: each is a versioned snapshot of core packages for one receiver. A package is complete, and its gate to MAD's automation tier opens, when a person has confirmed every required record and every record it reads (refs); a handoff, when every core package it draws on is complete. Which packages fit depends on the phase and the venture's situation: priors per phase with conditions (the need-now form, EE-028), facts from the records first and from the question matrix where the records are silent. Inside a package, a record moves on its own when nothing it reads first is still unconfirmed; otherwise it waits (records.after). Agents never come in a package: an agent that works a package is a package enhancement. Version 0.x: ours and unevaluated.

assumes.team: a solo founder or a small founding team (up to about five people)
assumes.note: Naive is opinionated (2026-10-28, EE-069): it assumes one governance model. The founders decide, confirm every record and do everything in the venture, product management and engineering included. How packages split and which gates hold follow from that model; other structures (separate engineering teams, boards that gate decisions, enterprises) are not modeled. Packages that matter only for them, or only after Validation, are kept here marked not_modeled and are left out of the venture package.

versions: A venture package gets a new version each time a package becomes complete or the phase changes; the manifest records it and, in a git repository, the tag to set (package/<venture>/v<n>). Ordinary edits stay plain commits.

enhancements.agents: An agent that works a package (drafts its records, keeps them current, acts on them) is a package enhancement. Naive's packages hold records only; Mentura and the founder's own agents enhance them. The hackathon demo includes routing and the harness agent's passes to show the enhancement.

questions.note: The question matrix: what a reasoning model answers about a venture to decide which packages fit it now. Each question sets one fact. A question is asked only in the phases it lists and only when the venture's records do not already settle the fact (from: records). Jev answers each as a typed noul question over the venture's records; an answer at or above 0.7 sets the fact, at or below 0.3 clears it, and anything between stays open for the founder.

items.ask: Is the venture raising money from investors now, or about to?
Does the venture have a public website, or plan one within the next month?
items.from: a site presence record (a site Naive has read)

items.ask: Is the product offered to partners or intermediaries who serve customers of their own?
Will the venture hire anyone, or bring on a cofounder, in the next three months?
items.from: the founder's flags (hiring) and the team decision

items.ask: Does the venture work in a regulated field (health, finance, education, legal, children, public sector)?
Does the founder mean to sell the venture or take it public one day?

note_split: Venture package definitions live in packages/<name>/package.json. This catalog holds the shared fit rules, the record dependency graph and the question matrix (EE-067, EE-069, EE-071).
